raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints such as `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` keep attention projections, shared experts and dense MLPs in BF16. This PR adds opt-in, load-time block-FP8 conversion for user-selected BF16 linears, so these layers can use FP8 GEMMs without exporting a separate checkpoint.

## Modifications

- **New option `--nvfp4-ckpt-fp8-dense-modules <module-or-pattern> ...`**, unset by default. It replaces the earlier boolean flag in this PR. Selected eligible BF16 linears are converted after loading to E4M3 with 128×128 weight blocks and dynamic per-token-group activation quantization. Layers the checkpoint already quantizes keep their configured method.
- **Selection reuses existing matching.** Literal module names and dotted paths use SGLang's module-path matching. `*` patterns use ModelOpt's checkpoint exclusion-pattern compiler. Fused projections must be selected through all of their checkpoint parts (for example `gate_proj up_proj`, not `gate_up_proj`); a partial fused selection is an error. Startup logs the rank-local count and warns about selectors that matched nothing.
- **Implementation stays in `modelopt_quant.py`.** `ModelOptOnlineBlockFp8LinearMethod` reuses the existing FP8 compute path and stores power-of-two scales when the selected DeepGEMM path needs UE8M0. `linear.py` registers its loader. There are no changes to `fp8.py` or to model implementations, and no model-specific defaults.
- **Draft/MTP and `lm_head` are not converted.** Draft construction is detected through the existing build scope, not layer names. Independent draft quantization options keep their behavior.
- **Online weight updates are rejected while the option is set**, on every pipeline stage, including stages with no matches. Begin/end update sessions check every selected runner before any restore or post-processing. This prevents writing BF16 values into FP8 storage under stale scales.
- **Docs:** server arguments, the ModelOpt quantization guide, and a GLM-5.2 cookbook example.

### Usage

The GLM-5.2 selection measured below:

```bash
--nvfp4-ckpt-fp8-dense-modules q_a_proj kv_a_proj_with_mqa q_b_proj o_proj wq_b gate_proj up_proj down_proj
```

A bare module name matches that module in every layer, so this selects the same 411 modules as the equivalent `'*.q_a_proj' '*.kv_a_proj_with_mqa' ...` patterns; the runs below used both forms. Patterns are for narrower selections, such as `'model.layers.*.self_attn.o_proj'`, and need quoting in the shell. This is an example to measure on your own GPU and parallelism, not a universal default. It leaves `kv_b_proj`, the indexer `wk`/`weights_proj`, and the draft model unconverted.

The option only touches linears the checkpoint leaves in BF16, that is, modules matched by `exclude_modules` in `hf_quant_config.json`. For `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (78 decoder layers: 3 dense, 75 MoE, plus MTP layer 78), this selection does the following to each excluded group:

| Checkpoint `exclude_modules` entry (BF16 in the checkpoint) | Converted to FP8 | Stays BF16 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model.layers.0*`, `model.layers.1.*`, `model.layers.2.*` (dense layers) | `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`, `indexer.wq_b`\*, `mlp.gate_up_proj`, `mlp.down_proj` | `kv_b_proj`, `indexer.wk_weights_proj`\* |
| `model.layers.{3..77}.self_attn*` (75 entries) | `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`, `indexer.wq_b`\* | `kv_b_proj`, `indexer.wk_weights_proj`\* |
| `model.layers.{3..77}.mlp.shared_experts*` (75 entries) | `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` | none |
| `model.layers.78*` (MTP / NextN draft layer) | none | all of it: draft layers are never converted |
| `lm_head` | none | `lm_head`: never converted |
| `model.embed_tokens` | none | embedding (not a linear layer) |
| Not excluded: routed experts in layers 3–77 | none | already NVFP4, unchanged |

\* Only the 21 layers with their own DSA indexer. Fused names are SGLang's: `q_a_proj` + `kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `gate_proj` + `up_proj`, `wk` + `weights_proj`. In total, 411 linear modules are converted, the same count on every rank, as checked by a full-model load audit.

**Small-batch trade-off.** Converting the fused A projection or `q_b_proj` makes them ineligible for SGLang's BF16 min-latency GEMM, so decode can be slower at small batches. An earlier measurement with the boolean flag showed ITL p90 6.28 → 7.02 ms at concurrency 1. Users can leave those modules out, or select them only on prefill workers.

**Note for reviewers: `SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_GEMM_IN_ATTN`.** This PR does not change that existing variable or its docs. The variable converts only `q_b_proj`, and only for DeepSeek-family models. For the main model, this option covers the same case (list `q_b_proj`) and more. The one difference is the MTP / NextN draft layer: the variable also converts its `q_b_proj`, while this option leaves draft layers at checkpoint precision. If both are set, the variable gives `q_b_proj` its own FP8 config, which bypasses the ModelOpt hook, so nothing is converted twice; in that case `q_b_proj` in the option's list matches nothing and logs a no-match warning. Whether to deprecate the variable in favor of this option is a separate follow-up.

## Tests

Based on `main @ e624174f0`. Unit tests were rerun on this commit; the full-model, accuracy and performance runs below used the same change on `main @ 302b78ccf`.

- **CPU:** 132 tests and 134 subtests passed (Linux, no skips). They cover dispatch, literal and wildcard selection, fused-part validation, argument docs, update-session rejection without mutating state, and draft construction. The new wildcard cases fail on the pre-change code.
- **CUDA (B300, SM103):** 10 tests and 6 subtests passed, no skips. Before rebasing, the same suite also passed on two nodes. They load BF16 weights through the registered loader (column, row and separately loaded merged projections, plus a ragged block), convert after loading, and compare the FP8 forward pass against BF16 by cosine similarity and relative error. They also cover a single-rank DCP replica and update rejection, each with both literal and wildcard selectors. They are registered for the H100/B200 CI lanes, which have not been run locally.
- **Selection parity:** replaying matching over 59,145 checkpoint matrix paths left existing exclusions and literal selections unchanged, and equivalent wildcard selections produced identical paths.
- **Full model (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, P/D):** all 16 target ranks converted 411 modules each with the option and none without it. All 16 draft ranks had zero converted modules, and the shared head stayed BF16. Eight P/D smoke cases passed in each arm (chat, a tool call with a follow-up, concurrent requests, streaming).
- Every touched test file passes when run the way CI runs it (`python3 <file> -f`), including `test_server_args_docs_coverage.py`. Repository pre-commit hooks and the docs build check (`mint broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects`, the version CI pins) pass.

## Accuracy

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on 8×B300, native TP8 with the model-card launch command (no DP-attention, no MTP). The two arms differ only in the option. CIs are paired 95% bootstrap intervals over problems.

### NVIDIA model-card suite

Settings follow the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max tokens 100K for GPQA and 64K for the rest.

| | GPQA Diamond | IFBench | AA-LCR | τ²-Bench Telecom | SciCode |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP8 baseline, NVIDIA model card | 89.52 | 74.95 | 69.38 | 97.90 | 49.85 |
| NVFP4, NVIDIA model card | 89.39 | 75.81 | 70.13 | 98.25 | 49.04 |
| NVFP4, option off (ours) | 89.84 | 77.33 / 79.67 | 66.50 | 97.37 | 46.99 |
| NVFP4, option on (ours) | 90.03 | 74.33 / 77.67 | 73.50 | 96.78 | 47.92 |
| On − off [95% CI] | +0.19 [−1.07, +1.45] | −3.00 [−7.33, +1.33] / −2.00 [−6.33, +2.33] | +7.00 [+1.50, +12.50] | −0.58 [−3.22, +1.75] | +0.93 [−2.12, +4.00] |

- **GPQA Diamond:** sgl-eval 0.1.3, 198 questions × 8 repeats, pass@1. Its prompt and answer extraction are the same as NeMo-Skills' Artificial Analysis (AA) prompt.
- **IFBench:** official harness, 300 prompts, one sample. Prompt-level accuracy is shown as strict / loose; AA reports loose.
- **AA-LCR:** v1.0 dataset and prompts, 100 questions × 2. The equality checker is Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 at temperature 0, which is AA v1.0's judge model.
- **τ²-Bench Telecom:** base split, 114 tasks × 3 trials, max 100 steps, pass^1. The user simulator is the same Qwen model, which matches AA's methodology.
- **SciCode:** official prompts with scientist background, 65 problems / 288 subproblems × 3 repeats, sub-problem accuracy (AA's headline metric). Generated code ran in a network-isolated sandbox with a 300 s per-step timeout (SciPy 1.13.1). Main-problem accuracy, which needs every step of a problem to pass, was 15.90 off and 12.31 on (−3.59 [−8.21, +0.51]); with 65 problems it is noisy. As a check of the grader, the public validation split's own reference solutions passed 48 of 50 steps. The two misses are dataset issues that affect both arms the same way: one reference picks its timestep from wall-clock timing and produces a different trajectory length than the stored target, and one differs numerically on a single case.

The AA-LCR gain (+7.0) is the only interval that excludes zero, out of eleven comparisons in this PR. With 100 questions it may be chance, and we don't present it as an improvement. NVIDIA ran four of these benchmarks on vLLM, and its exact harness configs are not public, so its rows are references rather than matched controls.

### Z.ai GLM-5.2-FP8 card settings

These follow the Z.ai footnote: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max 163,840 tokens. The math sets use Z.ai's system prompt with the problem as the user message, and are graded by "Exact Answer:" extraction (with `\boxed{}` as a fallback) plus symbolic equivalence. Z.ai used a GPT-5.5 judge. The math datasets are MathArena's copies, pinned to fixed revisions.

| | GPQA Diamond | AIME 2026 | HMMT Feb 2026 | HMMT Nov 2025 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GLM-5.2-FP8, Z.ai card | 91.2 | 99.2 | 92.5 | 94.4 |
| NVFP4, option off (ours) | 90.85 | 98.96 | 96.78 | 97.29 |
| NVFP4, option on (ours) | 91.22 | 97.92 | 96.78 | 96.04 |
| On − off [95% CI] | +0.38 [−0.88, +1.70] | −1.04 [−2.92, +0.83] | 0.00 [−1.70, +1.52] | −1.25 [−2.71, 0.00] |
| Repeats | 198 × 8 | 30 × 16 | 33 × 16 | 30 × 16 |

All runs completed every sample with no request errors. Most of the HMMT Nov gap comes from outputs hitting the 163,840-token limit (2 → 9 of 480). Wrong answers that ended normally were 11 vs 10. Our HMMT scores are above Z.ai's, which likely reflects the grading and dataset differences above rather than an improvement over FP8.

Taken together, we did not find a quality change beyond run-to-run noise. This does not rule out small regressions.

## Performance

16 B300 GPUs, prefill/decode disaggregated: two TP4/DP4 prefill workers (EP4) and one TP8/DP8 decode worker (EP1), with DP-attention and MTP. AIPerf 0.12.0 traffic: 124K input tokens (58K shared prefix plus 66K unique), 7K output tokens, streaming, temperature 0, `ignore_eos`. Each point sends traffic for 1,200 s, with up to 300 s to drain. Off and on use the same seed and identical input bytes at each point. One run per point.

**Request rate (Poisson):**

| Offered req/s | Completed / sent (off, on) | TTFT p50 off → on | TTFT p90 off → on | ITL p90 off → on |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.86 | 955/955, 955/955 | 7.12 → 6.27 s | 10.27 → 8.43 s (−18%) | 11.75 → 11.34 ms |
| 1.08 | 1314/1314, 1314/1314 | 8.31 → 6.88 s | 12.20 → 10.53 s (−14%) | 13.15 → 12.95 ms |
| 1.3 | 1582/1582, 1582/1582 | 23.61 → 10.16 s | 33.97 → 15.90 s (−53%) | 13.06 → 12.59 ms |

Every request completed in both arms. Up to 1.08 req/s, both configurations keep up with the offered load and the option lowers TTFT by 14–18% at p90. At 1.3 req/s, the prefill queue builds up without the option (TTFT p90 34.0 s); with it, TTFT p90 is 15.9 s. ITL is equal or slightly lower with the option at every rate.

**Closed loop, concurrency 64:**

| | TTFT p50 | TTFT p90 | ITL p50 | ITL p90 | Completed req/s | Requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Off | 7.36 s | 11.83 s | 8.50 ms | 10.61 ms | 0.876 | 1,113 |
| On | 6.51 s | 10.32 s | 8.24 ms | 10.42 ms | 0.908 | 1,157 |

Earlier kernel traces (boolean-flag revision, per 8K-token prefill step) show converted dense GEMMs at about 148 ms → 83 ms, plus 13 ms of FP8 activation quantization. Total time across the repeating layers is 511 → 453 ms.

## Limitations

- Concurrency 1–16 decode was not re-measured on this revision; see the small-batch trade-off above.
- Tested on B300 (SM103) only. A selection that pays off here may not on SM90 or under other parallelism, which is why there is no default.
- The CUDA tests cover a single-rank DCP replica, not multi-rank DCP.
- Online weight updates are rejected rather than supported.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests (CPU and CUDA).
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

After the first load, `layer.weight` is the same Parameter but holds FP8 data. An online weight update (`update_weights_from_disk` / `update_weights_from_tensor`) loads BF16 checkpoint values into it again. The row-parallel and merged-column loaders cast them straight to E4M3 with `copy_`, and this re-entry branch then treats them as already quantized with the old `weight_scale_inv`. The column-parallel loader (`copy_with_check`) instead raises "Downcasting not allowed" partway through the update.

**Example**

After a reload, `o_proj` serves raw E4M3 casts of the BF16 values times the stale block scales. The outputs are wrong and nothing reports an error.

**Fix**

Set `layer._derived_weight_cache_error` here so the weight updater rejects online updates with a clear message, or implement `restore_weights_before_loading` to bring back a BF16 weight.

+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    block_size: List[int],
+    pow2_scale: bool,

+    """Quantize a 2-D BF16/FP16 weight to E4M3 with one FP32 scale per block.

+    for the amax only.
+    """
+    block_n, block_k = block_size
+    n, k = weight.shape

+        w = torch.zeros((pn, pk), dtype=weight.dtype, device=weight.device)

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

The flag converts `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `q_b_proj` to FP8. `prepare_qkv_latent` and `q_b_proj_forward` use the min-latency `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` for 1-16 token batches only when `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible()` sees a BF16 weight. With the flag on, small decode batches lose that kernel and run FP8 DeepGEMM plus a separate activation-quant kernel.

**Example**

GLM-5.2's fused A weight (2624x6144) and its TP8 `q_b_proj` (2048x2048) are both eligible in BF16. The PR's table shows ITL p90 at concurrency 1 going from 6.28 ms to 7.02 ms (+12%).

**Fix**

Measure decode with these two modules excluded. If this path causes the regression, exclude them, or say in the docs that low-latency decode can get slower (for example, enable the flag only on prefill workers in PD).

**Issue**

This 10-line comment repeats the PR description's rationale. `.claude/rules/comment-style.md` asks for one or two lines and puts design rationale in the PR body or docs. The same applies to the docstrings of `Fp8OnlineBlockLinearMethod` and `quant_weight_block_fp8_online` in `fp8.py`, the 4-line block above `supports_online_fp8_dense` in `modelopt_quant.py`, and the 15-line module docstring of the new test.

**Fix**

Keep one short line per excluded module, for example `# kv_b_proj: copied to BF16 w_kc / w_vc before quant methods run.` Move the rest to the PR body.

**Issue**

The docstring says the DeepGEMM GEMM and the weight-loading path "are covered on-device", but the PR adds no GPU test. `Fp8OnlineBlockLinearMethod.create_weights`, `process_weights_after_loading`, and `apply` never run in CI, and no registered test turns the flag on.

**Fix**

Add a small CUDA test: build one linear layer with `Fp8OnlineBlockLinearMethod`, load a BF16 weight through its `weight_loader`, call `process_weights_after_loading`, and compare `layer(x)` with `F.linear(x, w_bf16)`. Register it on an NVIDIA suite, and fix the docstring.

detail.body:
## Motivation

ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints such as `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` keep attention projections, shared experts and dense MLPs in BF16. This PR adds opt-in, load-time block-FP8 conversion for user-selected BF16 linears, so these layers can use FP8 GEMMs without exporting a separate checkpoint.

## Modifications

- **New option `--nvfp4-ckpt-fp8-dense-modules <module-or-pattern> ...`**, unset by default. It replaces the earlier boolean flag in this PR. Selected eligible BF16 linears are converted after loading to E4M3 with 128×128 weight blocks and dynamic per-token-group activation quantization. Layers the checkpoint already quantizes keep their configured method.
- **Selection reuses existing matching.** Literal module names and dotted paths use SGLang's module-path matching. `*` patterns use ModelOpt's checkpoint exclusion-pattern compiler. Fused projections must be selected through all of their checkpoint parts (for example `gate_proj up_proj`, not `gate_up_proj`); a partial fused selection is an error. Startup logs the rank-local count and warns about selectors that matched nothing.
- **Implementation stays in `modelopt_quant.py`.** `ModelOptOnlineBlockFp8LinearMethod` reuses the existing FP8 compute path and stores power-of-two scales when the selected DeepGEMM path needs UE8M0. `linear.py` registers its loader. There are no changes to `fp8.py` or to model implementations, and no model-specific defaults.
- **Draft/MTP and `lm_head` are not converted.** Draft construction is detected through the existing build scope, not layer names. Independent draft quantization options keep their behavior.
- **Online weight updates are rejected while the option is set**, on every pipeline stage, including stages with no matches. Begin/end update sessions check every selected runner before any restore or post-processing. This prevents writing BF16 values into FP8 storage under stale scales.
- **Docs:** server arguments, the ModelOpt quantization guide, and a GLM-5.2 cookbook example.

### Usage

The GLM-5.2 selection measured below:

```bash
--nvfp4-ckpt-fp8-dense-modules q_a_proj kv_a_proj_with_mqa q_b_proj o_proj wq_b gate_proj up_proj down_proj
```

A bare module name matches that module in every layer, so this selects the same 411 modules as the equivalent `'*.q_a_proj' '*.kv_a_proj_with_mqa' ...` patterns; the runs below used both forms. Patterns are for narrower selections, such as `'model.layers.*.self_attn.o_proj'`, and need quoting in the shell. This is an example to measure on your own GPU and parallelism, not a universal default. It leaves `kv_b_proj`, the indexer `wk`/`weights_proj`, and the draft model unconverted.

The option only touches linears the checkpoint leaves in BF16, that is, modules matched by `exclude_modules` in `hf_quant_config.json`. For `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (78 decoder layers: 3 dense, 75 MoE, plus MTP layer 78), this selection does the following to each excluded group:

| Checkpoint `exclude_modules` entry (BF16 in the checkpoint) | Converted to FP8 | Stays BF16 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model.layers.0*`, `model.layers.1.*`, `model.layers.2.*` (dense layers) | `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`, `indexer.wq_b`\*, `mlp.gate_up_proj`, `mlp.down_proj` | `kv_b_proj`, `indexer.wk_weights_proj`\* |
| `model.layers.{3..77}.self_attn*` (75 entries) | `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`, `indexer.wq_b`\* | `kv_b_proj`, `indexer.wk_weights_proj`\* |
| `model.layers.{3..77}.mlp.shared_experts*` (75 entries) | `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` | none |
| `model.layers.78*` (MTP / NextN draft layer) | none | all of it: draft layers are never converted |
| `lm_head` | none | `lm_head`: never converted |
| `model.embed_tokens` | none | embedding (not a linear layer) |
| Not excluded: routed experts in layers 3–77 | none | already NVFP4, unchanged |

\* Only the 21 layers with their own DSA indexer. Fused names are SGLang's: `q_a_proj` + `kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `gate_proj` + `up_proj`, `wk` + `weights_proj`. In total, 411 linear modules are converted, the same count on every rank, as checked by a full-model load audit.

**Small-batch trade-off.** Converting the fused A projection or `q_b_proj` makes them ineligible for SGLang's BF16 min-latency GEMM, so decode can be slower at small batches. An earlier measurement with the boolean flag showed ITL p90 6.28 → 7.02 ms at concurrency 1. Users can leave those modules out, or select them only on prefill workers.

**Note for reviewers: `SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_GEMM_IN_ATTN`.** This PR does not change that existing variable or its docs. The variable converts only `q_b_proj`, and only for DeepSeek-family models. For the main model, this option covers the same case (list `q_b_proj`) and more. The one difference is the MTP / NextN draft layer: the variable also converts its `q_b_proj`, while this option leaves draft layers at checkpoint precision. If both are set, the variable gives `q_b_proj` its own FP8 config, which bypasses the ModelOpt hook, so nothing is converted twice; in that case `q_b_proj` in the option's list matches nothing and logs a no-match warning. Whether to deprecate the variable in favor of this option is a separate follow-up.

## Tests

Based on `main @ e624174f0`. Unit tests were rerun on this commit; the full-model, accuracy and performance runs below used the same change on `main @ 302b78ccf`.

- **CPU:** 132 tests and 134 subtests passed (Linux, no skips). They cover dispatch, literal and wildcard selection, fused-part validation, argument docs, update-session rejection without mutating state, and draft construction. The new wildcard cases fail on the pre-change code.
- **CUDA (B300, SM103):** 10 tests and 6 subtests passed, no skips. Before rebasing, the same suite also passed on two nodes. They load BF16 weights through the registered loader (column, row and separately loaded merged projections, plus a ragged block), convert after loading, and compare the FP8 forward pass against BF16 by cosine similarity and relative error. They also cover a single-rank DCP replica and update rejection, each with both literal and wildcard selectors. They are registered for the H100/B200 CI lanes, which have not been run locally.
- **Selection parity:** replaying matching over 59,145 checkpoint matrix paths left existing exclusions and literal selections unchanged, and equivalent wildcard selections produced identical paths.
- **Full model (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, P/D):** all 16 target ranks converted 411 modules each with the option and none without it. All 16 draft ranks had zero converted modules, and the shared head stayed BF16. Eight P/D smoke cases passed in each arm (chat, a tool call with a follow-up, concurrent requests, streaming).
- Every touched test file passes when run the way CI runs it (`python3 <file> -f`), including `test_server_args_docs_coverage.py`. Repository pre-commit hooks and the docs build check (`mint broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects`, the version CI pins) pass.

## Accuracy

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on 8×B300, native TP8 with the model-card launch command (no DP-attention, no MTP). The two arms differ only in the option. CIs are paired 95% bootstrap intervals over problems.

### NVIDIA model-card suite

Settings follow the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max tokens 100K for GPQA and 64K for the rest.

| | GPQA Diamond | IFBench | AA-LCR | τ²-Bench Telecom | SciCode |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP8 baseline, NVIDIA model card | 89.52 | 74.95 | 69.38 | 97.90 | 49.85 |
| NVFP4, NVIDIA model card | 89.39 | 75.81 | 70.13 | 98.25 | 49.04 |
| NVFP4, option off (ours) | 89.84 | 77.33 / 79.67 | 66.50 | 97.37 | 46.99 |
| NVFP4, option on (ours) | 90.03 | 74.33 / 77.67 | 73.50 | 96.78 | 47.92 |
| On − off [95% CI] | +0.19 [−1.07, +1.45] | −3.00 [−7.33, +1.33] / −2.00 [−6.33, +2.33] | +7.00 [+1.50, +12.50] | −0.58 [−3.22, +1.75] | +0.93 [−2.12, +4.00] |

- **GPQA Diamond:** sgl-eval 0.1.3, 198 questions × 8 repeats, pass@1. Its prompt and answer extraction are the same as NeMo-Skills' Artificial Analysis (AA) prompt.
- **IFBench:** official harness, 300 prompts, one sample. Prompt-level accuracy is shown as strict / loose; AA reports loose.
- **AA-LCR:** v1.0 dataset and prompts, 100 questions × 2. The equality checker is Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 at temperature 0, which is AA v1.0's judge model.
- **τ²-Bench Telecom:** base split, 114 tasks × 3 trials, max 100 steps, pass^1. The user simulator is the same Qwen model, which matches AA's methodology.
- **SciCode:** official prompts with scientist background, 65 problems / 288 subproblems × 3 repeats, sub-problem accuracy (AA's headline metric). Generated code ran in a network-isolated sandbox with a 300 s per-step timeout (SciPy 1.13.1). Main-problem accuracy, which needs every step of a problem to pass, was 15.90 off and 12.31 on (−3.59 [−8.21, +0.51]); with 65 problems it is noisy. As a check of the grader, the public validation split's own reference solutions passed 48 of 50 steps. The two misses are dataset issues that affect both arms the same way: one reference picks its timestep from wall-clock timing and produces a different trajectory length than the stored target, and one differs numerically on a single case.

The AA-LCR gain (+7.0) is the only interval that excludes zero, out of eleven comparisons in this PR. With 100 questions it may be chance, and we don't present it as an improvement. NVIDIA ran four of these benchmarks on vLLM, and its exact harness configs are not public, so its rows are references rather than matched controls.

### Z.ai GLM-5.2-FP8 card settings

These follow the Z.ai footnote: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max 163,840 tokens. The math sets use Z.ai's system prompt with the problem as the user message, and are graded by "Exact Answer:" extraction (with `\boxed{}` as a fallback) plus symbolic equivalence. Z.ai used a GPT-5.5 judge. The math datasets are MathArena's copies, pinned to fixed revisions.

| GLM-5.2-FP8, Z.ai card | 91.2 | 99.2 | 92.5 | 94.4 |
| NVFP4, option off (ours) | 90.85 | 98.96 | 96.78 | 97.29 |

| Repeats | 198 × 8 | 30 × 16 | 33 × 16 | 30 × 16 |

All runs completed every sample with no request errors. Most of the HMMT Nov gap comes from outputs hitting the 163,840-token limit (2 → 9 of 480). Wrong answers that ended normally were 11 vs 10. Taken together, we did not find a quality change beyond run-to-run noise. This does not rule out small regressions.

## Performance

16 B300 GPUs, prefill/decode disaggregated: two TP4/DP4 prefill workers (EP4) and one TP8/DP8 decode worker (EP1), with DP-attention and MTP. AIPerf 0.12.0 traffic: 124K input tokens (58K shared prefix plus 66K unique), 7K output tokens, streaming, temperature 0, `ignore_eos`. +import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+import sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant as mq
+from sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state import get_tp_group
+from sglang.srt.layers.linear import MergedColumnParallelLinear, RowParallelLinear
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import (
+    ModelOptFp4Config,
+    ModelOptOnlineBlockFp8LinearMethod,
+)
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.model_runner import _gather_block_fp8_linear
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.model_runner_components.weight_updater import (
+    _unsupported_derived_weight_cache_error,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils import get_device_sm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.layer_ut_utils import (
+    assert_output_close,
+    init_single_process_dist,
+    make_tp1_column_parallel_linear,
+)
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+# (M, N, K); N=192 leaves a ragged 64-row last weight block.
+SHAPES = [(5, 512, 1024), (64, 192, 512), (128, 2048, 2048)]
+MODULES = ["o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj"]
+
+
+def _nvfp4_config():
+    qc = ModelOptFp4Config.from_config(
+        {
+            "quantization": {
+                "quant_algo": "NVFP4",
+                "group_size": 16,
+                "exclude_modules": ["model.layers.*.self_attn*", "model.layers.*.mlp*"],
+            }
+        }
+    )
+    qc.update_packed_modules_mapping({})
+    return qc
+
+
+@unittest.skipIf(get_device_sm() < 90, "block-FP8 linear requires SM90+")
+class TestFp8OnlineBlockLinear(CustomTestCase):
+    modules = MODULES
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        init_single_process_dist()
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        patcher = mock.patch.object(
+            mq, "_online_fp8_dense_modules", return_value=self.modules
+        )
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+
+    def _load(self, layer, w, shard_id=None):
+        # Exercise the loader chosen by construction, not weight_loader_v2 directly.
+        self.assertEqual(layer.weight.weight_loader, layer.weight_loader_v2)
+        if shard_id is None:
+            layer.weight.weight_loader(layer.weight, w)
+        else:
+            layer.weight.weight_loader(layer.weight, w, shard_id)
+
+    def _check(self, layer, w, m):
+        self.assertIsInstance(layer.quant_method, ModelOptOnlineBlockFp8LinearMethod)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.weight.dtype, torch.bfloat16)
+        layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.weight.dtype, torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        x = torch.randn((m, w.shape[1]), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+        out, _ = layer(x)
+        ref = x.float() @ w.float().T
+        assert_output_close(self, out, ref, cos_threshold=0.995)
+        # Cosine alone misses a uniform scale error such as returning 2 * ref.
+        relative_error = (out.float() - ref).norm() / ref.norm()
+        self.assertLess(relative_error.item(), 0.08)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(out).all().item())
+
+    def test_column_linear(self):
+        for m, n, k in SHAPES:
+            with self.subTest(shape=(m, n, k)):
+                layer = make_tp1_column_parallel_linear(
+                    _nvfp4_config(), n, k, prefix="model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj"
+                )
+                w = torch.randn((n, k), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+                self._load(layer, w)
+                self._check(layer, w, m)
+
+    def test_row_linear(self):
+        layer = RowParallelLinear(
+            input_size=1024,
+            output_size=512,
+            bias=False,
+            params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            quant_config=_nvfp4_config(),
+            prefix="model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj",
+            parallel_group="replicated",
+        ).cuda()
+        w = torch.randn((512, 1024), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+        self._load(layer, w)
+        self._check(layer, w, 32)
+
+    def test_merged_shards_loaded_separately(self):
+        n, k = 1024, 1024
+        layer = MergedColumnParallelLinear(
+            input_size=k,
+            output_sizes=[n, n],
+            bias=False,
+            params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            quant_config=_nvfp4_config(),
+            prefix="model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj",
+            parallel_group="replicated",
+        ).cuda()
+        gate, up = (
+            torch.randn((n, k), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+            for _ in range(2)
+        )
+        self._load(layer, gate, shard_id=0)
+        self._load(layer, up, shard_id=1)
+        self._check(layer, torch.cat([gate, up]), 64)
+
+    def test_dcp_replica_matches_layer(self):
+        # The DCP gather re-runs post-load on the FP8 replica; it must not requantize.
+        layer = make_tp1_column_parallel_linear(
+            _nvfp4_config(), 1024, 512, prefix="model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj"
+        )
+        w = torch.randn((1024, 512), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+        self._load(layer, w)
+        layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+        replica = _gather_block_fp8_linear(layer, get_tp_group())
+        x = torch.randn((16, 512), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            layer.quant_method.apply(replica, x),
+            layer.quant_method.apply(layer, x),
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+
+    def test_online_weight_updates_rejected(self):
+        # Reloading BF16 values into the FP8 weight would serve them under stale scales.
+        model = torch.nn.Module()
+        model.o_proj = make_tp1_column_parallel_linear(
+            _nvfp4_config(), 512, 512, prefix="model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj"
+        )
+        w = torch.randn((512, 512), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        self._load(model.o_proj, w)
+        model.o_proj.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(model.o_proj)
+        error = _unsupported_derived_weight_cache_error(model)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(error)
+        self.assertIn("--nvfp4-ckpt-fp8-dense-modules", error)
